/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 25 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2926 (44)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4735 (92)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2166 (35)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1643 (2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 877 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market firmed today, with the BCI 182 5TC increasing by $840 to $42,945. The Pacific remained steady, supported by good volumes from miners and operators, while a tighter tonnage list helped underpin sentiment. The Atlantic also firmed, with stronger C3 fixtures and fresh demand emerging across both the Trans-atlantic and Fronthaul routes, although overall trading activity remained limited. On C5, the index slipped marginally by 0.115 to $14.470. Three miners were in the market, with bids and offers narrowing through the day. Following yesterday’s busy session, offers initially started in the upper $14s before one miner was reported bidding $14.00 and eventually fixing at $14.15. An operator was said to have paid $14.70 for slightly later dates, while a second miner was bidding $14.20 against offers around $14.60-$14.70. The Atlantic strengthened, with the C3 index rising by 0.909 to $37.091. Low $37s were reported fixed for end-September dates, highlighting a premium for later tonnage, while offers for around eta 11 September were still heard around $37.00.
PANAMAX
Cautious optimism as the P5TC rose another $318 to close at $19,496 today. Sources suggested a bit of a stand-off in the North Atlantic with Charterers reluctant to commit to anything above last done levels, with fronthaul enquiry outweighing trans Atlantic demand, mainly from the US Gulf. In the South the focus is now on second half September, with earlier vessels now beginning to feel the pressure a little, but with the Pacific remaining healthy Charterers are having to bid at last done levels without seeing much success as Owners hold firm for the time being. In Asia sentiment remained positive with the chance of more weather disruption adding to concerns of a tightening tonnage supply in the North, whilst Indonesian demand remained somewhat disappointing in comparison.
SUPRAMAX
Another lacklustre day with levels and sentiment seemingly unchanged and the 11TC average at $20,765, which was up only $24. In the Atlantic the Mediterranean continues to see a gradual decline in the fronthaul rate from Canakkale, whilst tonnage in the West Med at least has the option to ballast towards North Brazil. The Continent was said to be seeing fresh enquiry which is helping stabilize levels, whilst rates appeared to be static in North America and the South Atlantic, which both appeared fairly well balanced. There was talk of a Supramax fixed basis South West Pass for a trip Atlantic Colombia with grains in the low $20,000’s by Cargill and of an Ultramax fixed by Reachy delivery South West Pass for a trip with grains to China at $30,000. The Summer Lady (58,609 2013) fixed to Western Bulk delivery South West Pass with grains to the UK-Continent at $27,000 and the Omurtag (56,709 2012) fixed a coal cargo from North coast South America to the Baltic at $21,000 with Danbulk. The Doric Flame (63,520 2026) was rumoured to fixed a Javelin coal stem on voyage from Mobile to India at $55.00 fio but no further details emerged and the Astro Nembus (63,510 2017) fixed another coal stem from Mobile to India on timecharter at $32,000 with Swissmarine.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market continued to show signs of improvement, with brokers reporting a modest increase in activity. Overall, sentiment remains cautiously positive. While regional fundamentals remain mixed, tightening conditions in parts of the Pacific and improving confidence in the US Gulf have contributed to a firmer tone. The Baltic Handysize 7TC Index increased by 39 points to $15,794.

The US Gulf remains the strongest talking point, with brokers reporting increased cargo demand, firmer bids and improving sentiment, the Avalon Trader (40,569 dwt blt 2025) fixed an Altamira to Guayaquil trip at $21,000 daily. In contrast, the North Atlantic has shown signs of weakening, while the Mediterranean appears softer amid ample vessel supply. Market participants note that many Owners continue to favour backhaul employment, which has added pressure to rates. The Steel Magic (37,737 dwt blt 2016) fixed a Pacific South America trip at $16,750, and the Nestor I (32,312 dwt blt 2011) achieved $14,000 for a grain voyage from the US Gulf to the UK Continent.

In the Pacific, limited prompt tonnage in South East Asia has created some tightness, helping owners maintain firmer ideas. Chinese steel cargoes remain available, providing a degree of support and contributing to a more positive market tone. Fixture activity reflected the steadily improving sentiment. The Ken Voyager (38,362 dwt blt 2012) secured a Pacific round voyage via East Coast India at levels reported in the high $15,000's redelivery Penang.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Domestic Iron Ore Production

Chinese run-of-mine iron ore output fell 20.0% year-on-year to 67.2 Mt in July, the lowest monthly figure since February 2021, National Bureau of Statistics data show. Production in the year-to-July was down 8.7% from the same period last year to 536.1 Mt. All four major mining regions experienced year-on-year declines in July: Hebei (-23.7% to 28.2 M), Liaoning (-28.3% to 10.8 Mt), Sichuan (-30.4% to 5.9 Mt) and Shanxi (-6.6% to 3.4 Mt). The governments safety checks continued in July, with more stringent safety measures introduced in response to weather disruptions which impacted operational throughput, Argus reports.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape curve rallied higher through the session today. September was the main focus, trading between 42,000–44,000. Early activity was concentrated around 42,250–43,000 before the market pushed higher through the afternoon, reaching 43,750–44,000 into the close. The Oct gains were significant also with 45250 paid towards the end of the day and the Sep v Oct spread continued to widen and weaken down to a low of -1600. Q4 26 traded mainly between 42,000–43,250, with later business around 43,000–43,250. The Oct v Nov spread strengthened up to 2000 in size late on, together with Sep v Q4 up to 750. Q1 27 also moved higher, trading from 28,650 up to 29,750. Further out, Q2 27 traded up to 35,250, while Cal 27 changed hands between 32,400–32,700.

EQUIVALENT RANGE, SUPPORTING INDEX LEVELS. THE TIGHTER BALLASTER LIST CONTINUES TO PROVIDE A REASONABLE FLOOR, ALTHOUGH, AS ELSEWHERE, CURRENT DEMAND NEEDS TO HAVE ENOUGH DEPTH TO DRIVE FURTHER IMROVEMENTS. PAC SHORT THE PACIFIC MARKET IS SHOWING AN UNEVEN TONE SO FAR, WITH ALL THE THREE MAIN FOCUS ZONES DEVELOPING AT SLIGHTLY DIFFERENT SPEEDS. OVERALL CARGO ENQUIRY REMAINS HEALTHY, WITH A LONG LIST OF REQUIREMENTS IN THE MARKET, BUT THE PACE OF FIXING HAS BEEN SOMEWHAT SELECTIVE AS CHARTERERS CONTINUE TO ASSESS TONNAGE AVAILABILITY AND RATE IDEAS. AUS HAS CLEARLY EMERGED AS THE STRONGEST AREA SO FAR, WHILE INDO AND NOPAC ARE TAKING A LITTLE LONGER TO GAIN MOMENTUM. WITH THE PHYSICAL INDICES CONTINUING TO MOVE HIGHER, THE UNDERLYING SENTIMENT REMAINS SOMEWHAT POSITIVE, ALTHOUGH THE GAP BETWEEN THE STRONGER AND WEAKER BASINS HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY EVIDENT. THE INDO MARKET APPEARS TO BE LAGGING BEHIND THE WIDER PACIFIC, DESPITE A HEALTHY AMOUNT OF CARGO BEING CIRCULATED. WE ARE SEEING A LONG LIST OF CARGOES, BUT THE FIXING PACE HAS NOT FULLY TRANSLATED INTO STRONGER RATES YET, WITH SHIPS BEING COVERED AROUND $16K BKI HONG KONG. THERE CONTINUES TO BE A DECENT AMOUNT OF TONNAGE LOOKING AT INDO BUSINESS, WHICH IS KEEPING CHARTERERS FROM HAVING TO CHASE TOO AGGRESSIVELY AT THIS STAGE. HOWEVER, WITH THE CARGO LIST REMAINING SIZEABLE, ANY TIGHTENING IN PROMPT TONNAGE COULD QUICKLY PUT SOME UPWARD PRESSURE ON RATES. NOPAC HAS ALSO BEEN SOMEWHAT BEHIND, WITH FIXTURES BEING REPORTED AROUND THE HIGH $17K BKI CJK. THE KEY FEATURE HERE REMAINS THE IMBALANCE BETWEEN CARGO AND SUITABLE TONNAGE. WE ARE SEEING A REASONABLE LIST OF GRAIN REQUIREMENTS, BUT NOT ENOUGH FRESH GRAIN TONNAGE COMING FORWARD TO COMFORTABLY COVER THE AVAILABLE CARGOES. AT PRESENT, HOWEVER, THE MARKET IS STILL MOVING AT A MEASURED PACE AND HAS YET TO SHOW A DECISIVE PUSH HIGHER. AUSSIE CONTINUES TO BE THE CLEAR OUTPERFORMER IN THE PACIFIC, WITH FIXTURES SEEN AROUND $18K BKI CJK AND A NOTICEABLE PREMIUM DEVELOPING OVER BOTH INDO AND NOPAC. THE STRONGER PERFORMANCE APPEARS TO BE SUPPORTED BY A COMBINATION OF STEADY CARGO ENQUIRY AND COMPARATIVELY TIGHTER TONNAGE AVAILABILITY, ALLOWING OWNERS TO MAINTAIN A FIRMER STANCE. THE GAP BETWEEN AUSTRALIAN BUSINESS AND THE REST OF THE PACIFIC IS NOW QUITE SIGNIFICANT, AND THIS IS LIKELY TO REMAIN AN IMPORTANT FEATURE OF THE MARKET IN THE NEAR TERM. ON THE PAPER SIDE, FFA HAS REMAINED RELATIVELY FLAT, SUGGESTING THAT THE MARKET IS STILL WAITING FOR A CLEARER SIGNAL ON THE NEXT DIRECTION, DESPITE THE FIRMER PHYSICAL FUNDAMENTALS. MEANWHILE, THE PHYSICAL INDICES HAVE CONTINUED TO MOVE HIGHER SO FAR.
